_method.metric: interior-anchor recall at tolerance (fraction of baseline anchors with a perturbed anchor within T bp); region edges excluded
_method.note: PROBE only -- locked params unchanged in the grammar

_question: Are A4 shells/anchors robust sequence properties, or window-parameter / region-edge artifacts? (coordinate-read stability, T3.1+T3.4)
grade: POSITIONS ROBUST, COUNT IS A RESOLUTION CHOICE. (1) At neighboring W/step/smooth_radius and small edge crops, 93% of interior anchors recur within 2 kb -- the anchor POSITIONS are a real ~kb-scale property of the sequence, not a window artifact. (2) min_shell_bp is a granularity knob: doubling it to 10 kb keeps only 0.31x the anchors, BUT those survivors land on baseline positions (precision 0.879) -- a consistent NESTED subset, not relocation. So the anchor INVENTORY (and anchor_loops count) is resolution-dependent while the boundaries themselves are stable. (3) Anchor positions carry ~kb uncertainty, so a distance like 'nearest anchor 1065 bp' is ~1 kb-binned, not exact. Net: the coordinate read survives -- graded as a robust multi-scale skeleton with a resolution-set anchor count, not as exact per-bp coordinates.
